title: Joint angle calculation from optical markers and IMUs attached to the lower body
author: Wolfgang Teufl
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vwye7fw
materials: Figure 1: Coordinate systems and biomechanical model.

steps.title: Physical Setup and Marker Placement
steps.instruction: Prepare the participant and sensors for motion capture and inertial measurement.

substeps.instruction: Place retroreflective markers on the participant following the Leardini et al. protocol.
Mount each IMU in a 3D printed casing containing four retroreflective markers.
Define the reference frame G through initial OMC system calibration, leveled so that zG opposes gravity.
Ensure marker rigid body coordinate systems are constructed so their origins coincide with the IMU coordinate frames.

steps.title: Segment Pose Estimation from OMC Data
steps.instruction: Calculate the global position (S_i,t_G) and orientation (q_i,t_GS) of each segment i at time t using a constrained optimization approach.

substeps.instruction: Define n ≥ 3 linearly independent 3D point correspondences between local segment coordinate frames {p1:n_Si} and observed positions in G {pi,j,t_G}.
Minimize the error sum for each segment: err(S_i,t) = Σ ||S_i,t_G + R_i,t_GS p_j_Si - p_i,j,t_G||^2 / n.
Apply joint constraints to ensure segments remain connected, where a joint J = {i, j, k, l} connects p_j_Si and p_l_Sk in frame G.
Solve the constrained optimization problem for s segments and k joints over m frames using a weight parameter λ = 0.01 to adjust joint constraint influence.

steps.title: Handeye Estimation
steps.instruction: Calculate the rigid transformation (orientation q_BI) between the IMU coordinate frame (I) and the OMC rigid body frame (B).

substeps.instruction: Mount the IMU casings on a bar and rotate the bar in all directions within the tracking volume.
Collect a synchronized sequence of angular velocities measured by the IMUs (ω_I) and derived from the marker rigid body orientations (ω_B).
Calculate q_BI using the relationship ω_B = q_BI ω_I.

steps.title: IMU-to-Segment (I2S) Calibration
steps.instruction: Extract the relative orientation (q_SI) and position (I_S) between the IMU and the attached segment using a static neutral pose sequence.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the I2S orientation using the rotation sequence: R_SI = R_SG R_GB R_BI (where R_SG is OMC segment orientation, R_GB is OMC rigid body orientation, and R_BI is handeye orientation).
Calculate the I2S position using: I_S = B_S = R_SG(B_G - S_G) (where B_G is global rigid body position and S_G is global segment position).
Assume the calibration is fixed for subsequent calculations.

steps.title: Segment Pose Estimation from IMU Data
steps.instruction: Estimate segment poses from IMU data using sensor fusion.

substeps.instruction: Obtain initial IMU poses from OMC data and the handeye transformation.
Apply the sensor fusion method as described in Teufl et al.

steps.title: Joint Angle Decomposition
steps.instruction: Derive joint angles by decomposing the relative orientation between connected segments.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the relative joint orientation (e.g., for the right hip: q_RightHip_SS = q_Pelvis_SG ⊙ q_RightUpperLeg_GS).
Decompose the relative joint orientations into Euler angles following the order: flexion (θz), then abduction (θx), then internal rotation (θy).
